summary: The recent arXiv selection emphasizes hydrodynamic-frame consistency, lattice-driven finite-temperature gluon-matter response functions, FRG stability issues in high-density QCD models, conserved-current probes of hadronization, ALICE heavy-flavour pp baselines, quarkonium-pair fragmentation, and deployable normalizing-flow distillation for LHC trigger anomaly detection. The main caution is that ML-based compression sustainability claims remain too thinly documented in a short lightning-talk contribution.
strongest_paper: The hydrodynamic-frame correspondence paper is the strongest heavy-ion theory infrastructure item because it directly clarifies how frame conventions affect transport-coefficient comparisons while preserving physical mode attenuation.

papers.title: Correspondence between hydrodynamic frames, transport coefficients, and hydrodynamic modes in relativistic fluids
papers.abstract: The paper derives transformations between Eckart and Landau-Lifshitz frames, shows frame-dependent thermal conductivities in a baryon-rich nucleon gas, and verifies invariant sound attenuation.

papers.title: Lattice-data-driven specific heat and isentropic bulk modulus of SU(3) gluon matter at finite temperature
papers.authors: Wei Shen, Zhen-Yan Lu, Muhammad Waqas, Xun Chen, Zhi-Jun Ma, Guang-Xiong Peng
papers.abstract: A lattice-pressure-constrained effective-gluon-mass model is used to calculate finite-temperature response functions, including specific heat and isentropic bulk modulus across deconfinement.

papers.title: Negative diffusion in the Functional Renormalization Group flow for the Quark-Diquark Model
papers.authors: Johannes Poeplau, Ashutosh Dash, Dirk H. Rischke
papers.abstract: The authors identify negative diffusion in the FRG flow as a model-level source of oscillatory instabilities at low temperature and high quark chemical potential, then propose hyperdiffusion regularization.

papers.title: Heavy-flavour production and correlations in pp collisions: precision tests of pQCD and hadronisation with ALICE
papers.authors: Deependra Sharma, for the ALICE Collaboration
papers.abstract: A compact ALICE proceeding reports prompt D-meson, B0, rapidity-ratio, and D0-J/psi associated-production measurements in pp collisions relevant to heavy-flavour baselines.

papers.title: Tracing Vacuum Hadronization with Conserved Currents
papers.authors: Weiyao Ke, Hai Tao Li, Wanchen Li, Xiaohui Liu, Ding Yu Shao
papers.abstract: The paper proposes conserved-current moments of charge, baryon number, and strangeness in jets as flavor-resolved probes of vacuum pair production and hadronization.

papers.title: Production of quarkonium pairs via the fragmentation mechanism
papers.authors: Franco Barattini, Benjamin Guiot, Marat Siddikov
papers.abstract: The paper estimates single- and dihadron-fragmentation contributions to heavy-quarkonium-pair production using perturbative fragmentation modeling and CGC heavy-quark amplitudes.

papers.title: Distilling Normalizing Flows for Real-Time Anomaly Detection at the LHC
papers.authors: Tara P. A. Tahseen, Noah Clarke Hall, Nikolaos Konstantinidis, Paula Martinez Suarez
papers.abstract: A conditional normalizing-flow likelihood is distilled into lightweight FPGA-suitable decision-tree and quantized neural-network students for real-time anomaly detection with missing-feature handling.

papers.title: Green BOA: Determining the environmental break-even point for ML-based data compression
papers.authors: Caterina Doglioni, Akshat Gupta, Thomas Elliott, Hanzila Hussain, Sanjiban Sengupta
papers.abstract: A short lightning-talk contribution estimates when ML-based lossless compression may break even environmentally relative to storage savings.
